@graph.headline: How to Prosecute Every Inbound Lead Within 5 Minutes
@graph.description: Speed to lead is broken: 80% of inbound leaks every quarter. The AI SDR architectural pattern that produces 5-minute response at 100% prosecution rate.
@graph.keywords: speed to lead, inbound lead prosecution, 5 minute lead response, 80% inbound leak, ai sdr inbound, inbound conversion rate b2b

acceptedAnswer.text: Speed to lead is the time elapsed between an inbound lead's signal (form fill, demo request, content download, webinar registration) and the first qualified outbound touch from a sales representative or AI SDR. The industry-standard benchmark is under 5 minutes. Speed to lead is distinct from lead routing, which is the rules-based assignment of a lead to the correct rep; routing is usually instantaneous in modern CRMs, but the assigned rep's response is the slow step that produces the typical 4-to-24-hour delay.

mainEntity.name: Why does 5-minute response matter so much?

acceptedAnswer.text: The InsideSales.com Lead Response Management Study, replicated multiple times since 2007, shows leads contacted within 5 minutes convert at roughly 21 times the rate of leads contacted at 30 minutes. Conversion drops sharply by the hour and flattens after roughly one hour, after which timing stops mattering. The reason is buyer psychology: a buyer who just filled your form has 3 to 7 active vendor evaluations in flight, and the first vendor to engage with relevant context wins disproportionate share of the conversation.

mainEntity.name: How does an AI SDR achieve 100% lead prosecution?

acceptedAnswer.text: By removing the human capacity bottleneck. The AI SDR runs four steps in sequence on every inbound lead within seconds: signal classification (matching the lead to one of 6 default signal types), intent classification (assigning one of 5 intent categories based on signal + contact + ICP fit), research protocol (the Universal Research Protocol runs 20 minutes of equivalent research in seconds), and sequence enrollment (high-intent classifications enroll in same-day sequences with personalized first-touch within minutes). Result: 100% of inbound leads receive a qualified first-touch within the 5-minute window.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between speed to lead and lead routing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lead routing is the rules-based assignment of an inbound lead to the correct rep based on territory, vertical, account ownership, or round-robin distribution. Most modern CRMs route in seconds. Speed to lead is the elapsed time from form fill to the first qualified outbound touch from the assigned rep, which is usually much slower than routing because the human rep is busy. AI SDRs collapse the gap between routing and response by handling the first-touch directly within minutes; humans handle replies and qualification.

mainEntity.name: How do you measure inbound prosecution rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prosecution rate is the percentage of inbound leads that receive a qualified, timely first-touch response. The simple formula: leads receiving qualified response within 5 minutes divided by total inbound leads in the same period. With an AI SDR plus a properly configured CRM, this becomes a straightforward report: filter inbound leads created in the period, cross-reference against the AI SDR's sequence-enrollment timestamps, and calculate the percentage with a delta under 5 minutes. Working AI SDRs show 100% on this metric. Human-only teams typically show 15-30%.
